transcript:
This message comes from Angie. Angie has been helping homeowners find skilled pros
to get their home projects done well for over 30 years. For everything from minor repairs
to major remodels, find reviews, pricing, and booking at Angie.com or on the Angie app.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton. Tennessee Republican Governor Bill Lee
has put executions in the state on hold and called for a third-party review
to determine what caused the failed execution of Christa Pike last night. Pike's attorneys say
she's in critical condition after receiving two lethal injections. They're calling for the
governor to commute her death sentence after what they describe as cruel and unusual punishment.
Pike was sentenced to death for a murder she committed at age 18. She would have been the
first woman executed in Tennessee in more than 200 years. Catherine Sweeney with member station WPLN
was a media witness to the execution. Usually that takes 10, 15 minutes. It took 45 because
they had such a hard time getting needles into her. So eventually the curtains did open and she
was really lively and talking and singing for a long time. She should have started to look sedated
but didn't. They closed the curtain and usually that's when the doctor comes out and calls time
of death but he didn't. So they tried again, they opened the curtains, they did it all again
and that didn't go really any better. Catherine Sweeney from WPLN reporting. The
Trump administration is fighting a judge's order to build housing for homeless veterans in LA.
NPR's Quill Lawrence reports. LA has the most homeless vets in the country but it also has a
built-in solution, a 388-acre VA campus. A judge ordered housing to be built there but VA appealed
and lost at the Ninth Circuit Court. Now the Trump administration has won a delay while it considers
appealing to the Supreme Court. The delay means no decision until after midterm elections. There's
no reason for any delay of litigation that has gone on for far too many years. Mark Rosenbaum
represents the plaintiffs. The net result is that some 3,000 veterans including combat veterans
are going to live and die on the meanest streets of this community. The VA declined to comment on
pending litigation. In May 2025, President Trump ordered a 6,000-bed facility to be built in LA
but there's no sign of action on his executive order. Quill Lawrence, NPR News. Mortgage rates
are at their highest level in almost three years. The average 30-year fixed-rate mortgage is now
almost 7.3 percent and PR's Steven Bassaha reports. Mortgage interest rates often go up with the yield
on the 10-year Treasury note and that yield has been floating around a more than two decade high.
Mortgage rates are up a quarter of a percent from last week. John Diamond is an economist
at Rice University and he says the high cost of borrowing is having a bad lock-in effect on the
economy. People are staying put. That's going to slow down consumption growth but hopefully that
will eventually lead to lower inflation. The Federal Reserve will consider raising interest
rates again later this month to fight inflation. Steven Bassaha, NPR News. Major U.S. stock indexes
rose today but just slightly. This is NPR News. States and cities are suing the Trump administration
for repealing rules that limit planet warming greenhouse gas emissions from power plants.
They argue that gutting the protections will set the nation back decades and worsen the
climate crisis. The EPA has said the repeal would save the industry more than 300 billion
dollars in costs. Tensions between Eritrea and Ethiopia have skyrocketed since the recent
eruption of conflict in Ethiopia's northern Tigray region. Emmett Livingstone reports Eritrea has
severed diplomatic relations with its larger neighbor. Fighting has raged in northern Ethiopia
since the Tigray People's Liberation Front or TPLF returned to war against the government last week.
Ethiopia blames Eritrea as well as other countries for backing the armed group which fought a
devastating civil war with the Ethiopian government between 2020 and 2022. Ethiopia has closed its
embassy in Eritrea and expelled 10 Eritrean diplomats over what it called "direct and
indirect acts of hostility." Eritrea quickly hit back, severing all diplomatic relations
with Ethiopia the same day. The conflict in Tigray is reverberating across a fragile region.
There are fears it could spiral even further. For NPR News, I'm Emmett Livingstone. Scientists
warned that thawing permafrost in the Arctic is releasing large amounts of methane and carbon
dioxide, adding to global warming. The Arctic is warming four times faster than the rest of the
world. This process releases greenhouse gases from decomposing plants and animals that were once
trapped in the permafrost. This is NPR News from Washington. Stay tuned for the following
announcements and messages from our sponsors.

topics.text: Tennessee Governor Bill Lee halts executions, orders review of failed Christa Pike execution
Trump administration wins delay in case ordering VA housing for homeless veterans in LA
Mortgage rates reach highest level in almost three years at 7.3 percent
Stock market indexes rise slightly as investors assess economic conditions
States and cities sue Trump administration for repealing greenhouse gas emissions rules
Eritrea severs diplomatic relations with Ethiopia amid renewed Tigray conflict
Arctic permafrost thaw releases methane and carbon dioxide, accelerating global warming
